title: ResearchContext 2.0: the biological scope evidence must fit
description: A scientist narrowing the question before any search happens. 'Mature human alveolar macrophages in pulmonary fibrosis' is a different question from 'macrophages', and evidence from mouse bone-marrow-derived cells is not a weaker answer to the first question -- it is an answer to a different one. strictness decides what happens to evidence outside the scope: STRICT excludes it, PREFER shows it separately and labelled CONTEXT MISMATCH, OPEN applies no restriction. BioSense never silently generalises mouse to human, cell line to primary, or healthy to disease.

strictness.description: strict = evidence outside the scope is excluded. prefer = in-scope evidence ranks first; out-of-scope evidence is shown separately and labelled. open = no restriction.

states.description: developmental or activation state, e.g. mature, inflammatory, chronically stimulated

exclude.description: Things explicitly ruled out, e.g. 'mouse-only evidence'

applied.description: Provenance of the search itself: what was asked for, what was actually searched, and which restrictions could not be satisfied.
